answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, transferable token before it can earn fees or influence allocation. The protocol links rewards to verified work and slashes the bond when independent audits confirm fraud, making it costly to create many disposable identities: each needs capital locked up and risks losing it. The bond could be called sable, ocean, or jade; the name matters less than enforceable rules and audits. This raises the attack’s cost without assuming identities are impossible to fake.
